clue.text: Huge boat has an uncontrollable response

parts.note: a gig is a light rowing boat
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A ship's crew reacts with a huge, involuntary fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic is a straightforward synonym for enormous or vast in size.

clue.text: Person of great nobility — a duke — supporting stupid Australian

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit underneath the first

parts.note: galah is Australian slang for a fool, after the noisy cockatoo

explanation.surface: An aristocrat props up a foolish Aussie.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest knight of Arthurian legend, stands for a person of noble character.

clue.text: 27-0 — yuck!

parts.note: 27 points to the answer at 27 across, meaning zip or vigour, for which another word is go
the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lopsided score met with disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference leads to a synonym of that entry rather than the entry itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is sticky slime, the sort of mess that prompts disgust; also gush or slush.

clue.text: One thirty-two? Time I left — madly important

indicators.note: madly says the letters are tossed about wildly before being sorted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A time of 1.32 noted as someone dashes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' tells us T and I are removed: rearrange ONE THIRTY-TWO, leave out T and I, and the rest spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of note is significant or remarkable.

clue.text: Ham-fisted, I fold up half of it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pen or fold is an enclosure for sheep

indicators.note: half of takes the second of the two letters of the short word

explanation.surface: A clumsy person admits collapsing part of a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like a verb but is the sheep pen; 'up' turns PEN into NEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept and ham-fisted are both synonyms of clumsy or incompetent.

clue.text: Increase strength in part of leg

explanation.surface: Boosting power in a bit of the trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up a radio or heater raises its power; a turn-up is the folded hem at the bottom of a trouser leg.

clue.text: Exploited American man

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A Yankee taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Used, in the sense of taken advantage of, matches exploited.

clue.text: Number and name applied to fish net occasionally

parts.note: the comedy film A Fish Called Wanda gives the name for the fish
to net something is to gain it

explanation.surface: Labelling the fish and catching it periodically.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fish' is the one in the 1988 film title.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from time to time, every so often.

clue.text: Revenge for return on investment

explanation.surface: Getting even, or getting a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Payback means retaliation, and also the money recouped from an outlay.

clue.text: Letter from Greece about disturbance in Crete, and so on

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the Greek letter goes round the rest

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: disturbance in means the following word is stirred up

explanation.surface: A Greek note about unrest on Crete, and more.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means and the rest, used to cut a list short.

clue.text: OK — to a howler, they rarely turn a blind eye

indicators.note: rarely suggests something done in an unusual way, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Those who make a terrible blunder seldom get it overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' reads as an adverb in the sentence but signals the rearrangement of all fifteen letters of OK TO A HOWLER THEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberately ignore something wrong is to pretend not to see it, an idiom for wilful blindness.

clue.text: It's stupid, what I'd left out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone foolish wonders what they omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'left out' but is the anagram signal working on WHAT I'D LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lacking in wits, only half-sensible, is a colloquial way of calling someone foolish.

clue.text: Benefice given to good man, person presumably a doctor?

parts.note: a living is a church benefice
St, saint, is crossword shorthand for a good man
one means a person

explanation.surface: A clergyman's post passed to a decent fellow, apparently a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Stanley's greeting 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?', the missionary explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: David Livingstone was a Scottish medical missionary, famously greeted with a presumption that he was the doctor.

clue.text: Installed in sedan, perhaps — but not king or emperor

parts.note: something installed is in

indicators.note: but not tells us to take something away from the word just given

parts.note: a sedan is an example of a car
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A fitted car accessory, though not fit for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king or emperor' looks like one phrase, but 'or' splits them: king is R, emperor is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sapa Inca was the title of the supreme ruler of the Andean Inca empire.

clue.text: After rest, great dog overcomes cold having energetic fun

indicators.note: After places the following piece behind the word for rest

parts.note: a break is a rest

indicators.note: overcomes suggests one piece covering another, so the dog wraps round C

parts.note: a Great Dane is a giant breed of dog
C is short for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: After a nap, a big hound shakes off a chill and frolics.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakdance is an athletic street dance style with spins and acrobatics.

clue.text: Various birds start to eat

parts.note: divers are diving water birds, also called loons

indicators.note: start to points at the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A mixed flock of birds begins feeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means of many different kinds, a direct synonym of assorted or mixed.

clue.text: Capital destination for Gilpin

explanation.surface: Where a rider was heading in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowper's comic ballad John Gilpin tells of his runaway ride to the Bell at Edmonton, now in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital of Alberta, Canada, and the town Gilpin was bound for in Cowper's poem.

clue.text: Set aside each comment except the second

indicators.note: except the second means drop the letter in second place of the word given

parts.note: a remark is a comment

explanation.surface: Putting each remark to one side bar one.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as read gives 'set-end', a garble of 'second'; the second letter of REMARK, E, is the one removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to reserve them for a particular purpose, to allocate or put by.

clue.text: Henry's involved with gaming material

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry takes part in some gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a checked cotton fabric, a kind of cloth or dress material.

clue.text: Rubbish bin's lid found in outbuilding

indicators.note: found in says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a garage is an outbuilding

indicators.note: a lid is on top, so it means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bin lid turns up in the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is a synonym of refuse or waste.

clue.text: Original creation — insect in stone

parts.note: in Genesis Adam was the first man created
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A primordial bug preserved in rock, like amber.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant is an old name for a legendary unbreakable stone, later identified with diamond.

clue.text: Cause to which ultimate in punishment's applied

definitions.text: Cause to which ultimate in punishment's applied

indicators.note: applied puts that letter on to the front of the next piece
ultimate in picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.walkthrough: As an &lit, the whole clue also defines: treason was long a capital crime, the ultimate punishment.

clue.text: Flower came up

explanation.surface: A bloom emerged from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is a garden bloom; rose is also the past tense of rise, meaning ascended.

clue.text: Apparent how prisoner's statement may be used

definitions.text: how prisoner's statement may be used

explanation.definitionFit: Something conspicuous is plainly visible; the police caution warns that what a suspect says may be given as courtroom proof.

clue.text: Sunscreen is very important, spread on really early on

indicators.note: early on takes the opening letters of the words

explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a peak or shade that keeps sun out of the eyes.

clue.text: Several guns turned up — to get this?

explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue pictures hunters with guns out for a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, the quarry of a shooting party.

clue.text: Description of August, we may hope — it takes a long time

definitions.text: Description of August, we may hope

explanation.surface: Hoping for a sunny summer month that seems to last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally: a month made up of sunny days, as we hope August will be.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an extremely long period; literally, it pictures a whole month of bright summer days.
